# ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops Daily Update (Jul 22, 2026)
## OVERVIEW 
Today's development focused on enhancing fee vault configuration, updating Ink Mainnet's fee vault recipient, and refining CI processes. Significant progress was also made in addressing flaky tests and understanding ZK execution performance.

## KEY TECHNICAL DEVELOPMENTS

### Fee Vault Configuration and Updates
A new feature was added to allow in-place updates of L2 fee-vault predeploy configurations, including recipient, withdrawal network, and minimum withdrawal amount, via owner-gated setters ([#1504](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/pull/1504)). Additionally, the Ink Mainnet's fee vault recipient was updated from Gelato to OP Enterprise ([#1505](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/pull/1505)).

### CI/CD and Task Execution Improvements
An unnecessary override was removed from a batcher unsafe signer configuration ([#1507](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/pull/1507)). The CI process was also improved by pinning the `isNestedTask` fork to the task's `FORK_BLOCK_NUMBER` during simulations, ensuring more consistent testing environments ([#1506](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/pull/1506)).

## NEWLY OPENED PULL REQUESTS
No new pull requests were opened today.

## CLOSED ISSUES

### Flaky Test Resolution
The flaky test `TestSingleChainSuperFaultProofsFromOpNode` was closed today ([#21952](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/issues/21952)). The root cause was identified as a transient 10-second timeout in `sysgo.getSuperRoot` due to contention under CI load, which was resolved by refactoring the function to reuse polled responses and eliminate redundant RPC calls.

## NEW ISSUES
No new issues were reported today.

## ACTIVE ISSUES

### ZK Execution Support in vm-runner ([#18325](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/issues/18325))
Discussion today focused on benchmarking the `vm-runner` with mock proving mode for ZK execution. Benchmarks show that while running the super-range program in mock proving mode (real RISC-V emulation without proof generation) is slower than native execution, it is feasible. The primary concern is the memory usage, but the overall conclusion is that continuously checking the latest L2 head using the mock prover should be possible.

### Flaky Test: `TestSupernodeInteropChainLag` ([#19610](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/issues/19610))
This flaky test recurred today in `memory-all-opn-op-reth` despite a previous fix. The recurrence was noted in an unrelated branch, suggesting the underlying issue might persist or have resurfaced. The issue may warrant reopening if it continues to recur.

### Flaky Test: `TestNotTruncateDatabaseOnRestartWithExistingDatabase` ([#20649](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/issues/20649))
A new occurrence of this flaky test was reported today. The failure occurs at the baseline sanity check before any restart, due to a mismatch between the live safe head (per-L2-block) and the safe head DB (per L1 origin). A fix was previously diagnosed and implemented in a PR that was auto-closed, and a fresh PR ([#21975](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21975)) re-landing this fix is now open.

### Flaky Test: `TestSupernodeInterop_SafeHeadProgression` ([#20851](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/issues/20851))
This flaky test was observed again today, failing with an error indicating that the head did not advance. The occurrence was noted in an unrelated Go dependency-layering change, and a workflow rerun was triggered.

### Light-Sequencer Oscillation During Recovery ([#21964](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/issues/21964))
A new occurrence was logged today, upgrading this issue from a convergence-time problem to a correctness problem. The oscillation during recovery in a light sequencer configuration can lead to the sync-start recovery path relabeling a local fork as safe/finalized, even if it's incorrect. This was observed in a test where a transaction was missing from a block on the light sequencer's EL, despite the cross-safe gate passing. The mechanism involves engine resets flip-flopping between follow-source refs and locally-built blocks, ultimately force-setting safe and finalized heads to a local unsafe fork block. This highlights that height-based safety-label checks are insufficient to distinguish forks once recovery has relabeled the local fork.
